passeSimple-01.why: First-group verbs (-er) take -a in the third person singular passé simple: il entra. -it belongs to second-group and some third-group verbs; -ut to avoir / être / -oir verbs and the like, not entrer.

passeSimple-02.why: The passé simple of faire: il fit, ils firent. faisèrent is invented by applying first-group rules; fîtes is the second person plural (vous fîtes), while the subject les ouvriers is third person.

passeSimple-03.why: The passé simple of prendre: elle prit, ils prirent (the stem becomes pr-). prenit / prenut are both invented forms.

passeSimple-04.why: The passé simple of avoir: il eut, ils eurent. avèrent is an invented form; eûmes is the first person plural (nous eûmes).

passeSimple-05.why: The passé simple of venir: il vint, ils vinrent (a special -in- stem). vaincre → ils vainquirent; vendre → ils vendirent. Recognising these forms is key to reading literary/historical texts in CE.

passeSimple-06.why: The passé simple of être: il fut, ils furent; il fut nommé = il a été nommé (passive). faire → il fit; falloir → il fallut.

passeSimple-07.why: soudain introduces a sudden, one-off action → the passé simple sonna (the main narrative line). sonnait is the imparfait, used for background description, which clashes with soudain; sonnit is a wrong form.

passeSimple-08.why: Time and background description take the imparfait: il était minuit passé; the main-line event (se déclencha) takes the passé simple. fût is the imperfect subjunctive and can’t be used in an independent statement; été is a past participle and can’t be a verb on its own.

passeSimple-09.why: chaque matin expresses a habitual past action → the imparfait donnait; jusqu’au jour où elle disparut is a one-off event, in the passé simple. donna expresses a single action; donne is the present and doesn’t fit a past narrative.

passeSimple-10.why: The passé simple of croire: il crut, ils crurent. croître → ils crûrent (with a circumflex); courir → ils coururent.

passeSimple-11.why: The passé simple of conclure: il conclut, ils conclurent. concluèrent is invented from first-group rules; conclûmes is the first person plural.

passeSimple-12.why: The passé simple of mettre / remettre: il mit / il remit, ils remirent. remettit / remettut are invented forms.

passeSimple-13.why: In news and history, the passé simple corresponds to the spoken passé composé: fut annoncée = a été annoncée (a completed one-off event). était annoncée is the imparfait, for background or duration; sera is the future.

passeSimple-14.why: The passé simple of atteindre (and peindre, craindre and other -indre verbs): il atteignit, ils atteignirent. atteindirent / atteignèrent are wrong forms.

passeSimple-15.why: The first person plural passé simple of être: nous fûmes (with a circumflex). fumes, without the circumflex, is the present of fumer (tu fumes); fûtes is the second person plural (vous fûtes).
